compute.title: Auto-suspend options, idle gaps, resume wait and cache per warehouse
compute.requires: IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on the SNOWFLAKE database; MONITOR on the warehouses (SHOW WAREHOUSES lists only warehouses the role can see)

params.name: period_days
params.meaning: days of history the check looks at, counted back from the export date

params.name: warn_saving_credits
params.meaning: saving credits at the recommended setting: at or above this the row reads WARN

params.name: crit_saving_credits
params.meaning: the same that reads CRITICAL

params.name: min_gaps
params.meaning: gaps: least a row needs before it can flag

params.name: warm_cache_pct
params.meaning: percent of scanned bytes read from the warehouse cache at or above which the cache is worth keeping

params.name: warm_repeat_pct
params.meaning: percent of queries that repeat an earlier statement shape at or above which the cache is worth keeping

params.name: warm_gap_s
params.meaning: seconds: median gap at or below which the cache is worth keeping

compute.confidence_note: Not yet run on a live account.
compute.read_this: one row = one warehouse. Gaps between its queries are replayed against the current auto_suspend and against 60 s, 2, 5 and 10 min. idle_min_* = billed idle minutes (a gap is billed up to the suspend time), suspends_* = resumes that setting would cause. est_saving_* = possible saving versus now (an estimate capped at the metered idle credits, part of the idle waste, never added to it). gaps, median_gap_s and longest_gap_min describe the gaps between queries. resume_p50_s / p95_s = how long a resume took, from its STARTED event to the COMPLETED or WAREHOUSE_CONSISTENT event (WAREHOUSE_EVENTS_HISTORY); resume_wait_p50_s / p95_s = time queries waited for the warehouse to resume or provision (queued_provisioning_time). manual_resizes = RESIZE_WAREHOUSE events; dml_exec_pct = share of execution time in DELETE, UPDATE and MERGE. cache_pct_weighted = share of scanned bytes read from the warehouse cache, which a suspend empties; repeat_share_pct = queries that repeat an earlier statement shape; result_cache_pct = queries answered with no scan (result cache, kept through a suspend). keep_warm = keep_warm when the cache is worth a longer setting, else suspend_sooner. recommended_auto_suspend_s is 300 for keep_warm, 60 otherwise, and is empty when the current setting is already that short or the row is NOT_ASSESSED. est_saving_usd_list is the saving at that setting.
compute.healthy: status = OK when the recommended setting saves under warn_saving_credits
compute.investigate_if: WARN when the saving at the recommended setting >= warn_saving_credits; CRITICAL when >= crit_saving_credits; auto_suspend 0 or NULL (never suspends) bills every gap in full
actions: ALTER WAREHOUSE ... SET AUTO_SUSPEND = recommended_auto_suspend_s (config)
keep 300 s or more where keep_warm says the warehouse cache is reused (config)
where resumes are frequent and resume_wait_p95_s is high, group the work into fewer runs (config)

compute.title: Gen1 or Gen2: which warehouses to test, and whether a conversion paid off
compute.requires: IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on the SNOWFLAKE database; MONITOR on the warehouses (SHOW WAREHOUSES lists only warehouses the role can see)

params.name: period_days
params.meaning: days of history the check looks at, counted back from the export date

params.name: dml_pct
params.meaning: percent of run time in delete, update and merge at or above which a Gen1 warehouse is worth a Gen2 test (the same bar as the Gen2 hint of sf_wh_auto_suspend_tuning)

params.name: min_days
params.meaning: days a conversion needs on each side before it can be judged

params.name: warn_cost_up_pct
params.meaning: percent rise in credits per query after a conversion at or above which the row reads WARN

compute.confidence_note: Not yet run on a live account.
compute.read_this: one row = one standard warehouse. generation is its generation now. dml_exec_pct is the share of its run time in DELETE, UPDATE and MERGE, which Gen2 runs faster (the same measure as sf_wh_auto_suspend_tuning). Gen2 bills 1.35 times the Gen1 rate per hour (1.25 on Azure), so it pays only when the same work finishes over a quarter sooner. converted_at is the last generation change in the window (event reason CONVERT_RESOURCE_CONSTRAINT) and converted_to the generation it moved to. For a conversion, before and after are the days of the window on each side (the day itself left out): credits per day and per query from WAREHOUSE_METERING_HISTORY and QUERY_HISTORY, and same_shape_exec_change_pct, the change in run time of the statement shapes that ran on both sides. verdict: test_gen2 (a Gen1 warehouse at or over dml_pct), gen1_fits, gen2, gen2_not_offered (5X and 6X-Large), paid_off (credits per query fell after the move to Gen2), about_even, costs_more (rose by warn_cost_up_pct or more), back_to_gen1, too_soon. Context, not a saving: no $ here.
compute.healthy: status = OK unless a conversion made the same work cost more
compute.investigate_if: WARN when verdict = costs_more (credits per query rose by warn_cost_up_pct or more after the move to Gen2)
actions: test Gen2 on a test_gen2 warehouse for a week: ALTER WAREHOUSE ... SET GENERATION = '2', suspended first so the old and new clusters do not bill together (config)
for costs_more, compare the busy hours, then move it back with GENERATION = '1' if the work did not speed up (config)
after a move to Gen2, try one size down: faster runs can fit a smaller warehouse (config)

compute.title: warehouse idle minutes - compute credits that ran no query (possible waste)
compute.requires: IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on the SNOWFLAKE database; MONITOR on the warehouses (SHOW WAREHOUSES lists only warehouses the role can see)

params.name: period_days
params.meaning: days of history the check looks at, counted back from the export date

params.name: min_idle_minutes
params.meaning: counted idle minutes in the window below which the idle share alone never flags

params.name: warn_idle_pct
params.meaning: percent of compute credits that ran no query that flags WARN

params.name: crit_idle_pct
params.meaning: the same that flags CRITICAL

params.name: warn_waste_usd
params.meaning: possible waste in dollars that flags WARN at any idle share

params.name: crit_waste_usd
params.meaning: the same that flags CRITICAL

compute.confidence_note: Not yet run on a live account.
compute.read_this: One row = one warehouse that ran or was billed in the window. idle_credits = compute credits minus the credits Snowflake attributes to queries (WAREHOUSE_METERING_HISTORY), so it is the time the warehouse was running with no query in it, including the auto-stop wait after the last query. idle_minutes converts those credits at this warehouse's credits per hour for its size and generation, and est_wasted_usd_list prices them. It is POSSIBLE waste: a few idle seconds between two queries are normal and are part of it. Hours newer than 8 h (the attribution lag) and adaptive warehouses (no attribution) are left out. waste_reason says it in one line. The gaps and the auto-suspend options are in sf_wh_auto_suspend_tuning.
compute.healthy: status = OK - idle is below :warn_idle_pct percent of compute credits, or below :min_idle_minutes minutes in the window, and under :warn_waste_usd of possible waste (field heuristic).
compute.investigate_if: status = WARN or CRITICAL - at least :min_idle_minutes idle minutes and at least :warn_idle_pct (WARN) or :crit_idle_pct (CRITICAL) percent of compute credits idle, or possible waste at/above :warn_waste_usd (WARN) or :crit_waste_usd (CRITICAL) dollars at any share, so a large idle cost on a busy warehouse is flagged too. NOT_ASSESSED is not a pass: read not_assessed_reason and waste_reason.
actions: ALTER WAREHOUSE ... SET AUTO_SUSPEND to the setting sf_wh_auto_suspend_tuning recommends (60 s, or 300 s where the warehouse cache is reused) (config)

find what keeps the warehouse awake between queries: polls, BI refreshes, task schedules (free)

compute.title: Warehouses kept awake by tiny repeated polls
compute.requires: IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on the SNOWFLAKE database; MONITOR on the warehouses (SHOW WAREHOUSES lists only warehouses the role can see)

params.name: period_days
params.meaning: days of history the check looks at, counted back from the export date

params.name: min_runs_per_day
params.meaning: runs per day a repeated statement needs, on average, before it counts as a poll

params.name: max_exec_ms
params.meaning: median run time in milliseconds at or under which a repeated statement counts as a poll

params.name: warn_credits
params.meaning: credits kept awake at or above which the row reads WARN

params.name: crit_credits
params.meaning: the same that reads CRITICAL

compute.confidence_note: Not yet run on a live account.
compute.read_this: one row = one warehouse. A poll is one user's repeated statement shape (the same query_parameterized_hash) that runs at least min_runs_per_day times a day on average, takes at most max_exec_ms, and repeats sooner than the warehouse's auto-suspend, so each run arrives before the warehouse can suspend. The gaps between queries are replayed twice against the current auto-suspend (the same replay as sf_wh_auto_suspend_tuning): with every query, and without the polls. keepalive_hours is the up time the polls add; keepalive_credits prices it at the warehouse's credits per hour and is capped at its idle credits (compute minus the credits Snowflake attributes to queries). est_idle_context_usd_list is part of the idle $ of sf_wh_idle_minutes, never added to it or to any waste total. top_poll_* name the poll with the most runs: user, statement type, shape hash (never its text), median run time and the median seconds between its runs.
compute.healthy: status = OK when polls keep the warehouse up for less than warn_credits in the window
compute.investigate_if: WARN when keepalive_credits >= warn_credits; CRITICAL when >= crit_credits
actions: point health checks and connection keep-alives at a query that needs no warehouse (SELECT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), or the client's own keep-alive setting) (free)
poll less often than the auto-suspend, or move the poll to a serverless task or alert (config)
give polls their own X-Small warehouse with a 60 s auto-suspend (config)

compute.title: Pipeline writes that make interactive queries queue on a shared warehouse
compute.requires: IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on the SNOWFLAKE database; MONITOR on the warehouses (SHOW WAREHOUSES lists only warehouses the role can see)

params.name: period_days
params.meaning: days of history the check looks at, counted back from the export date

params.name: pipeline_hour_pct
params.meaning: percent of an hour's run time in pipeline writes at or above which the hour counts as a pipeline hour

params.name: min_queued
params.meaning: interactive queries that queued before a warehouse can flag

params.name: min_quiet_reads
params.meaning: interactive queries outside pipeline hours needed to compare the two

params.name: warn_lift
params.meaning: times more often interactive queries queue in pipeline hours than in other hours at or above which the row reads WARN

params.name: crit_lift
params.meaning: the same that reads CRITICAL, when at least 10% of interactive queries in pipeline hours queue

compute.confidence_note: Not yet run on a live account.
compute.read_this: one row = one warehouse. Pipeline work is INSERT, MERGE, UPDATE, DELETE, COPY, CREATE TABLE AS SELECT, multi-table INSERT and UNLOAD; interactive work is SELECT. Each UTC hour is a pipeline hour when pipeline statements started in it take at least pipeline_hour_pct of its run time and at least a minute. queued_pct_pipeline_hours and queued_pct_other_hours are the shares of interactive queries that waited for a busy warehouse (queued_overload_time) in pipeline hours and in the other hours; lift is the first over the second. A high lift means the pipeline crowds out the people and dashboards on the same warehouse: move or reschedule the pipeline rather than upsize the warehouse for everyone. queued_in_pipeline_hours_pct is the share of all interactive queue time that falls in pipeline hours. top_pipeline_user_name and peak_pipeline_hour_utc name the main writer in pipeline hours and the hour of day its queue is worst. verdict: pipeline_crowds_out, queue_from_reads (queueing with no lift), no_quiet_hours (pipelines run in nearly every hour with reads, so there is nothing to compare), no_queue, single_workload. Context, no $.
compute.healthy: status = OK when interactive queries rarely queue, or queue as often outside pipeline hours
compute.investigate_if: WARN when at least min_queued interactive queries queued, min_quiet_reads ran outside pipeline hours, and lift >= warn_lift; CRITICAL when lift >= crit_lift and at least 10% of interactive queries in pipeline hours queued
actions: run the pipeline on its own warehouse, sized for it, with a short auto-suspend (config)
move the pipeline out of the hours people query (free)
if both must share, allow a second cluster (MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT = 2, Enterprise edition) instead of a bigger size (config)

cost.title: Resource monitors on track to hit their quota before the cycle resets

cost.read_this: one row = one resource monitor (name). used_pct is used credits of the quota. The cycle is worked out from start_time and frequency; daily_rate is used credits divided by the days elapsed in the cycle (at least one), projected_pct is that rate over the whole cycle as a percent of the quota, and days_to_quota is how long the remaining credits last at that rate. has_suspend is TRUE when the monitor stops warehouses at some percent, not only notifies.
cost.healthy: status = OK when the monitor is below its quota and its projection for the cycle stays under it.

A monitor already at its quota reads OK here: sf_cost_resource_monitor_coverage owns that finding. NOT_ASSESSED when the monitor has no quota or no reset cycle.
actions: ask the warehouse owners whether the pace is expected before the month end (free)
raise the quota or move a heavy job to the next cycle, knowing the monitor will suspend warehouses at its limit (spend)

storage.title: Search optimization that may not pay
storage.requires: IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on the SNOWFLAKE database

params.name: period_days
params.meaning: days of history the check looks at, counted back from the export date

params.name: min_reads
params.meaning: reads: least a row needs before it can flag

params.name: poor_scan_pct
params.meaning: poor scan pct: value this check uses

params.name: warn_usd
params.meaning: usd: at or above this the row reads WARN

params.name: crit_usd
params.meaning: usd: at or above this the row reads CRITICAL

storage.confidence_note: Not yet run on a live account.
storage.read_this: one row = a table that spent search optimization (build/maintenance) credits in the window. read_queries counts queries that read it; avg_scan_pct is the partitions scanned by single-table queries (search optimization should keep point lookups well under 10%). usd_per_read is the upkeep per read. scans_helped and extra_pruned_pct are Snowflake's own count of scans that used the search access path and the share of partitions it pruned beyond natural order.
storage.healthy: status = OK when upkeep is under warn_usd, or the table is read min_reads times with avg_scan_pct under poor_scan_pct and, when the benefits view has rows for the account, some of its scans used search optimization.
storage.investigate_if: WARN when upkeep is warn_usd or more and the table is rarely read, still scans poor_scan_pct of partitions, or has no benefit rows while other tables do; CRITICAL at crit_usd with those signs.
actions: run SELECT SYSTEM$ESTIMATE_SEARCH_OPTIMIZATION_COSTS and check which columns the lookups filter on (free)
ALTER TABLE ... DROP SEARCH OPTIMIZATION, or limit it with ON EQUALITY(col) to the columns actually searched (config)
batch DML on the table so maintenance runs less.

storage.read_this: one row = one internal stage (named, table or user) with bytes on its latest day. finding is orphaned (the stage, its schema or its database is dropped but bytes remain), owner_gone (a user stage of a disabled or deleted user), stale (no file changed in stale_days) or ok. est_storage_usd_month is the stage's storage run-rate; est_saving_usd_month is the same figure on a flagged stage only.

storage.title: Tables paying for a lot of Time Travel
storage.requires: IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on the SNOWFLAKE database

params.name: min_tt_gb
params.meaning: tt gb: least a row needs before it can flag

params.name: warn_tt_pct
params.meaning: tt pct: at or above this the row reads WARN

params.name: warn_usd
params.meaning: usd: at or above this the row reads WARN

params.name: crit_usd
params.meaning: usd: at or above this the row reads CRITICAL

storage.confidence_note: Not yet run on a live account.
storage.read_this: one row = a live table that holds Time Travel bytes today. tt_to_active_pct compares the old row versions kept for undo/AT queries with the live data; a high share on a table with a long retention_time means a churny table (MERGE, full rewrite, TRUNCATE+INSERT) kept for many days. est_saving_usd_month_if_1_day assumes Time Travel bytes shrink in proportion to retention days.

lower it with ALTER TABLE ... SET DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS = 1 (or 0 for rebuildable tables), or set it on the schema/database (config)
load incrementally instead of rewriting the whole table so fewer versions are kept (engineering).

storage.title: Tables nobody has read
storage.requires: IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on the SNOWFLAKE database

params.name: idle_days
params.meaning: idle days: value this check uses

params.name: min_gb
params.meaning: gb: least a row needs before it can flag

params.name: warn_usd
params.meaning: usd: at or above this the row reads WARN

params.name: crit_usd
params.meaning: usd: at or above this the row reads CRITICAL

storage.confidence_note: Not yet run on a live account.
storage.read_this: one row = a live table of at least min_gb, older than idle_days, that no query read (directly or through a view) in the last idle_days. still_written = TRUE means a pipeline keeps loading it (last_altered inside the window) although nothing reads it, so it costs compute too. last_write_at is the last query that wrote it (ACCESS_HISTORY objects_modified) in the window; written_in_window = TRUE when either source shows a write, FALSE = neither read nor written, NULL when the table has no TABLES row and ACCESS_HISTORY shows no write (unknown). est_storage_usd_month counts active, Time Travel and Fail-safe bytes; est_saving_usd_month is what dropping it saves (flagged rows).
storage.healthy: status = OK when the unread table costs less than warn_usd a month.
storage.investigate_if: WARN when an unread table costs warn_usd a month or more; CRITICAL at crit_usd.
actions: ask the owner (table_owner) and check downstream tools that read via extracts or shares (free)
drop it, or first rename/revoke access for a grace period; for still_written tables stop the job that loads them (config)
for data kept for compliance, unload it to cheaper external storage and drop the table (engineering).

storage.title: Most and least used databases and schemas
storage.requires: IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on the SNOWFLAKE database

params.name: period_days
params.meaning: days of history the check looks at, counted back from the export date

params.name: warn_usd
params.meaning: usd: at or above this the row reads WARN

params.name: crit_usd
params.meaning: usd: at or above this the row reads CRITICAL

storage.confidence_note: Not yet run on a live account.
storage.read_this: one row = one live schema. read_queries / write_queries count queries that read a table in it (base, dynamic, Iceberg and external tables and materialized views, also through views) or wrote one (INSERT, MERGE, COPY, CTAS, ...), from ACCESS_HISTORY; readers / writers are distinct users. dml_rows counts rows changed in TABLE_DML_HISTORY (it also has Snowpipe loads). activity_rank orders schemas by total queries (1 = busiest). never_used = no read, no write and no DML rows in the window on a schema older than the window. est_storage_usd_month prices its tables' active + Time Travel + Fail-safe bytes.
storage.healthy: status = OK when the schema is read or written, or it is unused but nearly free.
storage.investigate_if: WARN when a schema older than the window had no read, write or DML and holds tables costing >= warn_usd a month; CRITICAL at crit_usd. NOT_ASSESSED when ACCESS_HISTORY is empty.
actions: ask the schema owner whether the unused schema still feeds anything outside Snowflake (extracts, shares) (free)
revoke access for a grace period, then drop it or make it transient (config)
archive cold data to external storage (engineering).

storage.title: Write-heavy tables where Time Travel and Fail-safe grow
storage.requires: IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on the SNOWFLAKE database

params.name: period_days
params.meaning: days of history the check looks at, counted back from the export date

params.name: min_rows
params.meaning: rows: least a row needs before it can flag

params.name: warn_churn_x
params.meaning: churn x: at or above this the row reads WARN

params.name: warn_usd
params.meaning: usd: at or above this the row reads WARN

params.name: crit_usd
params.meaning: usd: at or above this the row reads CRITICAL

storage.confidence_note: Not yet run on a live account.
storage.read_this: one row = one live table with DML in the window. rows_added / rows_removed / rows_updated are summed from TABLE_DML_HISTORY; churn_x_per_day = (removed + updated) per day divided by the table's current row_count, so 1.0 means the whole table is rewritten every day. Every rewritten micro-partition is kept for retention_time days of Time Travel plus 7 days of Fail-safe, which is what est_history_usd_month prices (time_travel_bytes + failsafe_bytes).
storage.healthy: status = OK when the table is small, rewrites little of itself, or its history is cheap.
storage.investigate_if: WARN when churn_x_per_day >= warn_churn_x on a table of >= min_rows rows whose Time Travel + Fail-safe costs >= warn_usd a month; CRITICAL when that history costs >= crit_usd.
actions: find the job behind the writes (full reload, MERGE on all rows, TRUNCATE+INSERT) (free)
lower DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS, or make a rebuildable table TRANSIENT to drop Fail-safe (config)
switch the load to incremental or append-only, or cluster so MERGE touches fewer partitions (engineering).
